newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russia defence minister sees new reform route.
newsitem.headline: New Russia defence minister sees new reform route.

text.p: Russia's new defence minister, General Igor Sergeyev, is seeking "unorthodox methods" to reorganise the armed forces, his spokesman was quoted as saying on Monday. He gave no details.

The spokesman, General Anatoly Shatalov, told Interfax news agency that Sergeyev, former commander of the strategic missile command, "is counting on the support of allies and partners and avoiding confrontation".

Differences of opinion among military and civilian defence planners and among different branches of the forces, as well as a severe lack of money, have dogged efforts to begin slimming down and modernising Russia's vast army and fleet.

Sergeyev was in favour of "consolidating" the work of the various defence planning bodies, including the Defence Ministry and President Boris Yeltsin's two policy units, the Defence Council and the Security Council.

It was at a Defence Council meeting last Thursday that Yeltsin launched a surprise public attack on the ministry's failure to carry out big reforms and sacked Sergeyev's predecessor, Igor Rodionov, on the spot.

Sergeyev would also continue the struggle against corruption in the military, his spokesman said. Several top generals face graft charges and some are being held in custody as part of a crackdown on suspected widespread abuses in the armed forces.
